newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize mixed, other grains mostly steady in Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Maize mixed, other grains mostly steady in Budapest.

text.p: The grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) registered its highest turnover in three weeks on Wednesday in balanced trade, the BCE and dealers said.
But BCE official Zsolt Merenyi said, "This turnover is only outstanding looking back at the last few weeks, otherwise it would be below average."
Total grains turnover was 950 contracts or 390 million forints, the bulk of the contracts equally divided between maize and milling wheat.
Old (1996) crop maize futures eased 100 forints per tonne for May to end at 18,100 forints and July closed at 17,570 forints, down 130 and traders said they expect the downward trend to continue.
"I think prices should go lower as no fundamental changes happened," said Robert Vajo of Termin.
Hungary has large excess stocks of maize it cannot export partly due to lack of immediate demand and party to relatively high domestic prices.
New (1997) crop maize prices rose by a small margin, with December closing at 19,060 forints, up 60, but Vajo said that taking into account inflation, old and new crop prices are roughly equal.
Hungarian inflation was 18.8 percent year-on-year in February and the government targets a 17 percent inflation for this year.
Milling wheat prices were little changed on Wednesday in a balanced market, Vajo said.
"Traders took a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the long (Easter) weekend but they are also waiting for new information to trade on," he said.
